dedupe_keys.name: open311 georeport v2 open standard api for civic issue reports

description: Open311 is a collaborative open standard for civic issue tracking that lets people, apps and governments exchange non-emergency service requests. It began with an API for Washington, D.C.'s 311 system and grew into a community with San Francisco, OpenPlans, Code for America and others. GeoReport v2, the finalised and frozen specification, covers location-based issues such as graffiti, potholes and street cleaning through two resources, services and service requests, plus an optional token resource, with methods to list services and their definitions, post a request, and query one or many requests. A wiki page lists servers that implement it for particular jurisdictions, alongside developer libraries and supporting products. Coverage: any city that runs a compliant server. Access: free specification; data access depends on each city's endpoint. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: the specification is stable, but the site notes that compliance of implementations is still being verified. Simulation uses: a common schema for pulling street and public realm issue reports from several cities into one model. Related records: NYC 311 requests and FixMyStreet, which uses Open311.
